name: Patpatar
catalog_citation: SIL PNG Branch. 2004 [data checked by Ed and Debi Condra 1997]. Organised Phonology Data: Patpatar Language [GFK], Namatanai - New Ireland Province. Ukarumpa: SIL. 4 pp. (PDF 'Printed: September 6, 2004').
catalog_quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress is basically on the last syllable of a word. Exceptions: long vowels are always stressed, suffixes don't take stress, certain word classes don't take ultima stress, fully reduplicated words are almost evenly stressed, the high vowel of a high+low seguence is stressed, and open syllable intr. verbs and derived nouns usually take penultimate stress.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: verbatim confirmed on PDF p..), section 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)'; it is the only stress statement in the 4-page document. (2) Deciding source: an SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (1997 data, printed 2004) -- first-hand but a template summary, effectively a sketch; the classification 'weight-hedged' (final default, long vowels always stressed, lexical/morphological exceptions, CVC unaddressed) is a faithful reading of that paragraph and nothing seen contradicts it. (3) It is not the best available description: Glottolog lists Condra 1989 Patpatar grammar essentials (189 pp., same author, scan exists at MPI) and Peekel 1909 (216 pp., HathiTrust full view).
